status_summary: Bills are pending in the 119th Congress: the Legal Workforce Act (H.R. 251, introduced 2025-01-09) would, by its title, make E-Verify use mandatory and permanent; the House Judiciary Committee ordered H.R. 2641, the Day 1, Dollar 1 E-Verify Act, reported on 2026-01-08 (per CBO it would require all federal contractors and subcontractors to use E-Verify); and the Mandatory E-Verify Act of 2026 (S. 4620) was introduced on 2026-05-21. None has been enacted, and no executive order requiring E-Verify for all government contractors was found. The Federal Acquisition Regulation already requires E-Verify in covered federal contracts above certain thresholds, a rule that predates 2025.

timeline.event: Rep. Calvert introduced the Legal Workforce Act (H.R. 251) to make E-Verify mandatory and permanent.
The House Judiciary Committee ordered H.R. 2641, the Day 1, Dollar 1 E-Verify Act, reported; CBO's estimate describes it as requiring federal contractors and subcontractors to use E-Verify.
Sen. Britt introduced the Mandatory E-Verify Act of 2026 (S. 4620), described as requiring all employers to use E-Verify and permanently establishing it.

title: Make E-Verify permanent and mandatory, and require it for government contractors
